Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash.
 



 We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. In 2017, we launched a mobile app in Senegal for cash deposit, withdrawal, and peer\-to\-peer and business payments. Now, we have millions of users across 9 countries and are growing fast.
 



 Our goal is to make Africa the first cashless continent and that's where you come in...

**Description**
 At Amazon, our SCOT Labs team owns and operates the experimentation platform that powers randomized controlled trials (RCTs) across Supply Chain Optimization Technologies (SCOT). We are the scientific gatekeepers for policy updates that govern how Amazon buys, stores, and moves billions of units of inventory worldwide. This is not traditional A/B testing: we are building the infrastructure and methodology to causally evaluate complex and interconnected supply chain interventions.
   

  

 Our platform runs experiments that span millions of products and hundreds of fulfillment nodes simultaneously, measuring the real\-world impact of policy changes on inventory health, customer experience, and operational cost. We are also advancing the science of causal inference in supply chain settings by developing novel approaches to treatment effect estimation, interference modeling, and emulation techniques that allow us to assess policy impact faster and more accurately than ever before.
   

  

 The experiments you design and the methods you build here will directly determine which policies ship to production. These decisions influence hundreds of millions of dollars in weekly inventory investments, labor allocation for tens of thousands of associates, and Amazon's overall supply chain efficiency. Beyond operational impact, this team pushes the frontier of causal experimentation methodology and contributes to the broader scientific community with publications at top venues.
   

  

 If you are a scientist who wants to shape how one of the world's largest supply chains makes decisions — solving causal inference challenges in real\-world settings no academic lab or startup can replicate — this is the team for you.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

* Partner with customer teams to design rigorous large\-scale experiments (such as randomized controlled trials and quasi\-experiments) to evaluate policy updates and model improvements across millions of products, hundreds of fulfillment nodes, and diverse business contexts
* Build and maintain production\-grade experimentation infrastructure and analytical tools using Python, SQL, Scala, and related technologies
* Advance causal inference methodology for supply chain settings, including treatment effect estimation, interference modeling, and emulation techniques that accelerate policy evaluation. Ensure these methods are supported by both theoretical foundations and empirical evidence.
* Translate complex research findings into clear insights and actionable recommendations for technical and non\-technical stakeholders at all levels.
* Contribute to Amazon's scientific community and the broader external research field through collaboration and publication in top\-tier venues.


 A day in the life
   

  

 You might start the morning digging into results from a randomized trial running across millions of products, deciding whether the estimator you built last month is holding up and where it breaks. By the afternoon you could be designing the next experiment with a partner team where clean randomization is not available, because treated and control units draw on the same fulfillment network and inventory pools, and you need an approach that stays credible despite the spillover.
   

  

 The role sits between developing methods and shipping them. You will build estimators and experiment designs for problems without textbook answers, prototype them in Python on real supply chain experiment data, and then put the ones that work into the platform other SCOT scientists use, writing Python, Scala, and SQL at a scale most scientists never encounter. You will also build supply chain emulation systems that replicate inventory dynamics end to end, so a design can be stress tested before it touches the real network.
   

  

 The problems are open, the data is unmatched in scale, and the methods you build will shape how scientists across SCOT think about causal inference and move billions of dollars in inventory decisions. If you want to do measurement and experimentation research that actually ships, this is where you do it.
   

  

**About The Team**
 The Forecasting and Labs Science team sits at the heart of Amazon's supply chain, building the science that determines what products are available, when, and at what cost for hundreds of millions of customers around the world. Our mission spans two deeply connected frontiers: pushing the boundaries of large\-scale time series forecasting through foundation models that generalize across an enormous and diverse catalog of products, and building the experimentation and causal inference methodology that rigorously evaluates whether supply chain policy changes should ship to production.
   

  

 We are a team of scientists who care deeply about both research rigor and real\-world outcomes. We don't just publish: we ship. And we don't just ship: we measure, iterate, and raise the bar. On the forecasting side, we build foundation models at a scale unmatched in industry, running experiments across millions of products and exploring novel data generation techniques that open new frontiers in model generalization. On the experimentation side, we design and run randomized controlled trials across hundreds of fulfillment nodes, advance causal inference in settings where interference is unavoidable, and build supply chain emulation systems that can evaluate policy changes in hours rather than months. Our work spans the full lifecycle: from foundational research and large\-scale experimentation to production deployment and downstream impact measurement across supply chain, inventory, and financial planning.

**Description**
 Millions of sellers list products on Amazon. You'll own the services that tell them what a valid listing needs, get their submissions live, and explain what to fix when one fails.
   

  

 Selling on Amazon comes down to three things a seller has to get right: learn what a valid listing needs, get it submitted, and fix it when something goes wrong. We build for all three, in every marketplace where Amazon operates. Some of our services tell a seller what their category requires before they submit, and whether their product is already in our catalog. Others take listings in and update them, one at a time or thousands at once in a bulk feed, and carry them through to a live offer. When something breaks, ours are the services that say what went wrong, in the seller's own language, while there's still time to fix it.
   

  

 You'll work on software that every seller and every seller tool passes through. The problems are API design, concurrency, event\-driven processing, and data modeling over a catalog whose rules shift by product, by marketplace, and by seller. You'll own what you build, from design through production and the on\-call rotation that follows, on a team cutting years of overlapping systems down to fewer and simpler ones. There's room to grow into owning a system end to end.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

* Own features end to end, from understanding what the customer needs through design, code, tests, deployment, documentation, and the operations that follow. This includes refactoring and removing software, not only writing new software.
* Design solutions to difficult problems where the goal is clear but the implementation is not. Reduce them to the simplest design that works, and review that design with senior engineers before you build it.
* Operate what you build. Take part in an on\-call rotation, hold the line on the latency and availability sellers depend on, drive issues to a permanent root cause fix, and automate recurring work instead of absorbing it.
* Document how your systems are built, tested, secured, and operated, and train new engineers on them. Give useful review feedback to engineers at every level, including engineers more senior than you.
* Work with the customers and partner teams that depend on your services, and make priority calls between new features, operational work, and business commitments. Keep your tools current, including AI\-assisted development, and stay accountable for the quality of everything you ship.

 You Join a Team Of Six To Twelve Engineers, With a Manager And Senior Engineers Who Read Your Designs And Your Code. A Typical Day Looks Like This

* Writing, testing, and debugging code for ongoing projects
* Reviewing code and incorporating feedback from your team
* Collaborating on technical solutions in design and architecture reviews
* Working with stakeholders to understand requirements
* Monitoring existing systems and resolving production issues
* Documenting technical specifications and processes
* Learning and applying new technologies and best practices


 Sellers are on the other end of all of it. A change you write this month is something a seller runs into next month, and the feedback comes back fast.
   

  

**About The Team**
 Our customers are the sellers who list products on Amazon, the software companies that build tools for them, and the internal teams that serve them. Sellers should not have to learn how Amazon works internally in order to sell on Amazon, so we absorb that complexity instead of passing it to them. Our teams together cover the full path a listing takes: creating and updating listings, defining what a valid listing requires and what already exists in the catalog, and telling sellers what is wrong and what to do about it.

 You'll write solutions, review AI outputs, and provide the expert\-level feedback that makes AI coding assistants smarter, safer, and more reliable. This is hands\-on engineering work at the frontier of AI development — not theoretical, not bureaucratic, and not boring.
   

  

 This is a fully remote, flexible contract role. If you can write clean code and explain your reasoning, we want to hear from you.
   

  

* Organization: Alignerr
* Type: Hourly Contract
* Location: Remote
* Commitment: 10–40 hours/week


**What You'll Do**
* Write, debug, and optimize code across a range of languages, frameworks, and problem domains
* Review and evaluate AI\-generated code for correctness, efficiency, readability, and best practices
* Identify bugs, logic errors, security issues, and performance bottlenecks in AI outputs
* Provide structured, detailed feedback explaining why code works — or doesn't
* Design challenging coding prompts and edge\-case scenarios to stress\-test AI capabilities
* Compare and rank multiple AI\-generated solutions based on engineering quality
* Work independently and asynchronously — fully on your own schedule


**Who You Are**
* Proficient in one or more programming languages (Python, JavaScript, Java, C\+\+, Go, TypeScript, or similar)
* Solid understanding of data structures, algorithms, and software design principles
* Able to read, write, and reason about code with clarity and precision
* Strong problem\-solving instincts and a systematic debugging approach
* Clear written communicator — you can explain technical decisions in plain language
* Self\-motivated and reliable when working independently without supervision
* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field — or equivalent practical experience


**Nice to Have**
* Experience across multiple languages or tech stacks (full\-stack, backend, systems, data engineering)
* Familiarity with AI/ML concepts, LLMs, or prompt engineering
* Background in code review, technical writing, or mentoring junior developers
* Experience with cloud platforms, DevOps, or distributed systems
* Competitive programming, open\-source contributions, or side projects that demonstrate your craft
* Advanced degree in Computer Science or related discipline


**Why Join Us**
* Work on cutting\-edge AI projects alongside leading research labs
* Fully remote and flexible — set your own hours and work from anywhere
* Freelance autonomy with intellectually stimulating, high\-impact work
* Directly influence how AI writes, understands, and reasons about code
* Sharpen your own engineering skills by evaluating diverse problems daily
* Potential for ongoing work and contract extension as new projects launch

**Company Description**
 At Autoscience Institute, we create AI systems that autonomously conduct AI research. Recently, we announced the first AI agent to autonomously create peer\-reviewed literature (ICLR 2025 Workshops). We are passionate about pushing the boundaries of artificial intelligence and contributing to groundbreaking advancements
   

  

**Role Description**
 We’re looking for a full\-time on site role for a Forward Deployed Engineer to bring AutoScience into the most important machine learning environments in the world.
   

  

 You’ll work directly with customers to understand their ML systems, deploy AutoScience into their infrastructure, and turn ambiguous modeling problems into environments where our automated researchers can run thousands of useful experiments.
   

  

 This is not a traditional solutions engineering role. You’ll write production code, work inside real ML pipelines, debug distributed systems, reason about machine learning challenges, and collaborate directly with our research and engineering teams to make the core product better.
   

  

 You’ll own deployments end\-to\-end from the first technical conversation to the first model improvement shipped into production.
   

  

**Qualifications**
* You’re an unusually strong engineer who likes operating where the problem is poorly specified. You bring strong interpersonal judgment and communication skills, build trust with teammates and stakeholders, and collaborate effectively across different working styles and areas of expertise.
* You get enjoyment from socializing with technical and non\-technical customers
* You should be comfortable opening an unfamiliar ML repository, understanding how the system works, getting it running, identifying what matters, and shipping something useful quickly.


 You likely have:
   

  

* Strong software engineering fundamentals and excellent Python skills.
* Experience building, training, evaluating, or deploying machine learning systems.
* Experience working with production cloud infrastructure and containerized workloads.
* Strong debugging skills across software, infrastructure, data, and ML systems.
* Experience owning technically complex projects from an ambiguous starting point through production.
* Good judgment about when to build something robust and when to move quickly.
* The ability to communicate deeply technical ideas with researchers, engineers, and technical leaders.
* An eagerness to spend significant time working directly with customers.
* A high degree of autonomy and comfort working in a fast\-moving environment.


**Benefits \& Perks**
* Our comp is competitive against major LLM frontier lab packages
* Unlimited PTO and flexible working arrangements
* Conference attendance and publication support


**Our Culture**
 We're a team of passionate researchers and engineers working to automate scientific discovery. We believe in the power of AI to accelerate scientific discovery and are committed to responsible AI development.
   

  

 We are an e\-verify employer.

We’re always looking for diverse, talented, service\-oriented people to join our exceptional team.

**Who We Are**
 Aurora’s mission is to deliver the benefits of self\-driving technology safely, quickly, and broadly.
   

  

 The Aurora Driver will create a new era in mobility and logistics, one that will bring a safer, more efficient, and more accessible future to everyone.
   

  

 At Aurora, you will tackle massively complex problems alongside other passionate, intelligent individuals, growing as an expert while expanding your knowledge. For the latest news from Aurora, visit aurora.tech or follow us on LinkedIn.
   

  

**What We Are Looking For**
 Aurora hires talented people with diverse backgrounds who are ready to help build a transportation ecosystem that will make our roads safer, get crucial goods where they need to go, and make mobility more efficient and accessible for all.
   

  

 We are seeking a ML Engineer to join the Behavior Planning Team. This is a high\-impact role where you will sit at the frontier of autonomous vehicle technology. You won't just be applying AI and ML methods; you will be advancing the state\-of\-the\-art for how a self\-driving system reasons about the world, interacts with humans on the road, and masters complex, high\-dimensional decision\-making.
   

  

**In this role you will**
* Define the architecture of our onboard planning models: Develop and deploy large\-scale models trained with Imitation Learning and Reinforcement Learning that enable the Aurora Driver to navigate complex environments with human\-like fluidity and superhuman safety.
* Revolutionize evaluation: Develop powerful offboard critic models that can evaluate driving behavior at scale, identifying subtle nuances in comfort, progress, and safety that traditional heuristics miss.
* Build our next\-generation simulation engine: Architect cutting\-edge offboard foundation models that power our simulation engine, creating realistic "world models" to test the Aurora Driver against an infinite variety of edge cases.
* Bridge research and production: Reach new frontiers of autonomous driving technology by pushing forward the state\-of\-the\-art, but also deploy your models on real production vehicles that drive on public roads and must meet the highest standards of safety.


**Required Qualifications**
* BS, MS, or PhD in Robotics, Machine Learning, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.
* 2\+ years of experience developing state\-of\-the\-art ML models, either in a research or production setting.
* Hands\-on experience working on Imitation Learning or Reinforcement Learning applied to physical or simulated agents.
* Experience training large models on massive datasets using distributed computing.
* Fluency in Python, with a focus on writing high\-performance, maintainable code.
* Deep experience with PyTorch (preferred) or another modern ML framework, and a mastery of modern ML architectures including Transformers and Diffusion Models.


**Desirable Qualifications**
* A track record of publications in top\-tier ML conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, CoRL, CVPR, AAAI).
* Experience deploying complex ML systems in production environments.
* Experience in developing generative models or neural simulators for synthetic data generation.
* Fluency with C\+\+, with a focus on writing high\-performance, safe, and maintainable code.

**Description**
 AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end\-to\-end products that surprise and delight out\-of\-the\-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.
   

  

 Amazon WorkSpaces has protected and empowered enterprise work for over a decade and we are now reimagining what a workspace is. We are building Agentic WorkSpaces: a platform where the workspace itself is an active partner in how you work not just infrastructure that delivers applications. Today more than a million users rely on WorkSpaces daily; tomorrow those workspaces will host AI agents alongside humans agents that code, troubleshoot, analyze, and act on behalf of their users governed by the same identity and security policies as the people they serve. We compete with Microsoft Citrix and Omnissa and we intend to leapfrog them by building the workspace that was designed for the agentic era not retrofitted for it.
   

  

 Agentic WorkSpaces' Data Plane is the connective tissue that makes this possible: the single entry point through which every WorkSpaces connection flows and the streaming backbone that delivers the desktop experience once a session begins. We own the end\-to\-end pre\-session journey authentication across every identity method, session authorization, resource discovery, gateway selection, and cross\-region failover as well as the in\-session streaming stack that carries pixels to the user and the pipeline that delivers workspace health and performance metrics back to our customers.
   

  

 Our vision is for that connection to be seamless and invisible: users and the agents working beside them reach their workspace instantly and securely sessions stream with high fidelity and low latency failover is transparent and the health of every connection is observable through the same AWS tools customers already use delivered reliably from commercial regions to classified partitions at a scale where availability and security are non\-negotiable.
   

  

 We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to design build and operate the services that authenticate authorize connect and stream WorkSpaces sessions for humans and increasingly for the AI agents that work beside them across every supported identity provider and streaming protocol. You will own end\-to\-end delivery of features and systems within the Data Plane from design through deployment and operations holding a high bar for availability latency and security on the services that stand between every customer and their workspace.
   

  

 You are customer\-obsessed technically deep and energized by solving hard problems. You think big about what the workspace of the future looks like a connection fabric that treats humans and agents as first\-class principals streaming that adapts intelligently to network conditions and brokering that routes and heals itself before users notice a problem and then you build the systems to get there.
   

  

 You thrive in ambiguity make sound trade\-off decisions with incomplete information and hold yourself accountable for results that matter. You want to solve challenging problems in distributed systems identity real\-time streaming and network infrastructure at a scale that impacts more than a million users daily.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

* Design and deliver features and systems within the Data Plane contributing to the architecture strategy for how the connection and streaming layer evolves to broker and stream sessions for AI agents alongside human users.
* Drive the work that unifies and simplifies how sessions are brokered and streamed across protocols making a consistent high\-fidelity connection experience the default. Partner with compute identity providers networking and gateway teams earning trust by driving technical discussions that result in impactful architectural decisions.
* Design and implement pre\-session authentication authorization and governance for a world where humans and agents share the same connection path: identity integration across every authentication method session authorization and access policies that treat agents as first\-class principals and a security posture built in rather than bolted on.
* Own the operation of low\-latency high\-availability brokering and streaming services that are the single entry point for more than one million WorkSpaces users globally. Ensure your services meet stringent SLAs across multiple production regions AWS partitions and streaming protocols with self\-healing routing transparent cross\-region failover and autonomous issue resolution before customers are impacted.
* Drive engineering excellence through instrumentation automated testing and pipeline\-based deployment eliminating manual toil and delivering a consistent connection and streaming experience across every protocol. Think big about the agentic era and experiment boldly with AI\-powered capabilities such as intelligent gateway selection self\-diagnosing connections and AI\-assisted operational management.
* Raise the bar on connection reliability and observability so that authentication session brokering high\-fidelity streaming and customer\-facing metrics are delivered without imposing an operational tax on the customer or the agent workflows running on the desktop.

**Research Engineer, Synthetic Data**
**About The Role**
 As a Research Engineer on the Synth Data team at SpaceXAI, you’ll invent and scale the synthetic data that teaches our models new capabilities. You own the full loop: spotting a capability the model is missing, designing a data generation strategy, building reliable pipelines and verifiers, and validating that the resulting data actually moves the model.
   

  

 You form hypotheses about what data will help, build the systems to produce it at scale, run ablations, and read the resulting traces and training signals to understand why it worked (or didn’t). Your datasets go directly into frontier training runs, and shape the development of Grok models.
   

  

 What you’ll work on
   

  

* Designing end\-to\-end synthetic data recipes that turn raw sources (traces, documents, codebases, workflows) into large, diverse, verifiable task sets.
* Building strong verification and anti\-hacking mechanisms so rewards are simple to compute and hard to game.
* Controlling difficulty and diversity so data stays learnable and reflects real usage instead of collapsing into templates.
* Running targeted ablations and analyses that demonstrate a dataset caused a capability improvement (and ruling out grader or data artifacts).
* Iterating from traces and training results to close specific gaps, then turning successful one\-off recipes into reusable infrastructure.
* Partnering with research and other RL Data teams to translate model capability goals into concrete synthetic data plans.


 You may be a fit if
   

  

* You have research experience on synthetic or post\-training data, in industry or academia. You've designed a data generation method, shipped the data into training, and can show its impact to the model you’re training.
* You have strong software engineering fundamentals and have built non\-trivial data pipelines, agent systems, or evaluation frameworks.
* You have taste for what makes a good training task: hard enough to teach something real, simple enough to grade reliably, and resistant to reward hacking.
* You are careful and systematic — understanding both aggregate metrics and close reading of raw outputs.
* You enjoy turning messy, open\-ended problems into repeatable, high\-quality data production systems.


 Applying

Make it rain. Make Snow. Make Earth Habitable. 
 


  


 Rainmaker builds and deploys audacious technologies that work with nature to create an abundant, habitable planet. We are modernizing proven cloud\-seeding science with weather\-resistant UAS, radar and satellite observations, numerical weather prediction, novel sensing and validation systems, and sustainable seeding technologies. We are building an integrated system to make more freshwater available to farms, ecosystems, and communities.
 


  


 Our ambition is bold, but we pursue it with humility. We take on difficult problems in the real world with technical rigor, grit, integrity, and an openness to learning and course\-correcting. We are hiring individuals with evidence of exceptional ability. If you want to build systems that endure, restore, and deliver the future we were promised, we want to hear from you.
 


  

 The vehicle software team builds the software that operates Rainmaker’s cloud\-seeding vehicles, connecting flight control, onboard computing, sensors, payloads, and ground operations. We work closely with electrical, mechanical, manufacturing, and flight operations teams to turn new hardware into reliable systems that can be built, deployed, and operated at scale. Our goal is to make every vehicle a dependable tool for delivering more freshwater where it is needed.
 




  




**About the Role** 
 You will own embedded firmware across Rainmaker’s vehicle and its integration with our onboard and ground control software systems. Your scope includes flight\-controller firmware, power distribution, sensor and payload controllers, and the interfaces connecting those systems to onboard Linux software. You will take work from architecture and board bring\-up through testing, manufacturing, deployment, and support in the field. We’re looking for a high\-agency engineer who identifies what needs to happen, turns incomplete requirements into a clear plan, and follows through until the hardware works reliably in real operating conditions. This is a hands\-on technical ownership role with the autonomy to shape the firmware architecture and the responsibility to deliver it.
 
  




**What You'll Do** 
  

  
* Own the architecture, implementation, and maintenance of all embedded firmware across the vehicle, including flight\-controller firmware, power distribution, sensors, and seeding payloads.
  
* Set firmware priorities, identify reliability risks and technical gaps, and drive projects from an ambiguous problem to a validated release.
  
* Bring up new boards with electrical engineers: read schematics, validate interfaces, write drivers, and debug failures at the boundary between hardware and software.
  
* Develop dependable device communication and command handling over CAN, UART, SPI, and I2C, with clear contracts for telemetry, timing, and fault behavior.
  
* Integrate firmware with our vehicle software so commands, device state, and telemetry behave consistently from the microcontroller to the operator.
  
* Design and validate safe startup states, watchdogs, interlocks, and recovery behavior for resets, communication loss, sensor faults, and interrupted updates.
  
* Own firmware builds, versioning, flashing, over\-the\-air updates, and recovery workflows so deployed vehicles run known, traceable software.
  
* Build automated tests, simulation, and hardware\-in\-the\-loop coverage that catch regressions and exercise failure modes before releases reach the fleet.
  
* Partner with manufacturing and flight operations to make provisioning, calibration, diagnostics, and servicing repeatable and practical.
  
* Investigate bench and field failures using logs, telemetry, and lab instruments; resolve root causes and turn what you learn into better software and tests.
  

  


  


  




**What We're Looking For** 
  

  
* 3\+ years of hands\-on experience developing embedded software or firmware for microcontroller\-based systems, including board bring\-up, hardware integration, and deployment into production or field use.
  
* Demonstrated ownership of an embedded subsystem from design through release and ongoing support, including making technical decisions independently, validating behavior on hardware, and resolving failures in real operating conditions.
  
* Strong systems programming skills in Rust and/or C/C\+\+, with the ability and willingness to work across both Rust and C/C\+\+ codebases.
  
* Practical experience with peripheral drivers and communication buses such as CAN, UART, SPI, and I2C.
  
* Comfort reading schematics and using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and hardware debuggers to isolate problems across electrical and software boundaries.
  
* The ability to reason about system failures and implement robust state machines, fault detection, safe outputs, and recovery paths.
  
* Experience building maintainable firmware with version control, reproducible builds, automated testing, and disciplined release practices.
  
* Evidence of high agency: you surface problems without waiting to be assigned, make sound decisions with incomplete information, ask for help when it matters, and close the loop on results.
  
* Clear communication and the ability to work closely with hardware engineers and operators, explain tradeoffs, and document decisions so others can build and service what you ship.
  

  


  


  




**What Will Set You Apart** 
  

  
* Experience with drones, robotics, aerospace, or other systems where software controls physical equipment in demanding conditions.
  
* Familiarity with PX4, MAVLink, flight\-controller development, or flight\-critical software.
  

  


  


  




**What Success Looks Like In the First 90 Days** 
 You have mapped the vehicle’s firmware, hardware interfaces, build and update paths, and most consequential reliability risks, and the team has a clear plan for what to address first. You can independently build, flash, instrument, and debug the key embedded systems and trace their behavior through our vehicle software. You have delivered a meaningful firmware improvement through bench and integration testing into an operational release, working with flight operations to verify its behavior in the field. You have improved at least one recurring source of friction in testing, provisioning, updates, or diagnostics, and established a practical ownership and release cadence for the firmware stack.
